headline: Morningstar's analysts say leading AI labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI are building lasting competitive advantages, though not yet fully formed.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: read in full, but it is one research firm's forecast, not a new event.
importance_line: What changed is that a major research firm is publicly arguing that AI labs can earn lasting profits, which matters first to savers and funds weighing Anthropic's expected stock listing, then to the chip, power and data-center suppliers whose spending depends on that, and the doubt is that this is Morningstar's own forecast, built on early figures, and it says the advantages are not yet fully formed.
summary: Morningstar, the investment research firm, says in the first of a three-part series started ahead of Anthropic's expected stock-market listing that leading AI labs are building economic moats (lasting competitive advantages), from a data-and-product feedback loop and a cost advantage at very large scale, though it says these moats are not yet fully formed. It argues profits will grow as running models for users (inference) becomes a bigger share of spending than training them, and says Anthropic reached a 5% operating margin on $11 billion of first-quarter 2026 sales.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text. The Anthropic margin figures are Morningstar's statement; the text does not tie them to a filing. The text carries a standard disclosure that its authors own shares in securities mentioned.
